item.content:encoded: Le borse europee sono in leggero calo trascinate al ribasso dai titoli tech, mentre gli investitori attendono dettagli sulle sanzioni che gli Stati Uniti hanno minacciato di imporre contro l’Iran, attesi nel corso della seduta. ** Intorno alle 9.40 l'indice paneuropeo Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) è in calo dello 0,1% a 653,65. ** Gli Stati Uniti hanno minacciato l’Iran con quella che hanno definito "la più grande offensiva finanziaria mai messa in atto", preparandosi a varare sanzioni economiche mirate ai partner commerciali dell’Iran; dal suo canto l’Iran ha detto che si impegnerà a bloccare tutte le esportazioni di greggio dal Golfo "se la guerra economica dovesse continuare". ** I titoli energetici (.SXEP) registrano un calo dello 0,5% seguendo l’andamento dei prezzi del Brent , che si attesta a circa 92,8 dollari il barile. ** Il comparto delle risorse di base (.SXPP) registra invece la migliore performance con un rialzo dello 0,7% grazie all’aumento dei prezzi dell’oro sull’indebolimento del dollaro. ** Il settore tech (.SX8P) è intanto in allerta in vista dei risultati di Nvidia (NVDA.O) attesi mercoledì, poiché gli investitori sono consapevoli di quanto sarà difficile per il produttore di chip soddisfare le aspettative spropositate. ** Gli operatori di mercato sperano inoltre di ottenere indizi sulle prospettive dei tassi di interesse Usa quando venerdì il presidente della Federal Reserve Kevin Warsh interverrà a Jackson Hole, in Wyoming.

item.title: For Republicans, Dallas convention is both rally and rescue mission
item.description: The Republican Party is increasingly viewing its first-of-a-kind midterm convention in Dallas next month as crucial to regaining momentum at a time when opinion polls show voter frustration over the economy and the Iran war, according to party officials, donors and convention planners.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Layne, Steve Holland
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump 's Republican Party is increasingly viewing its first-of-a-kind midterm convention in Dallas next month as crucial to regaining momentum at a time when opinion polls show voter frustration over the economy and the Iran war, according to party officials, donors and convention planners. When Republicans [USN:L1N432124 TEXT:"announced the convention"] earlier this year, some strategists dismissed it as a distraction as campaigns entered the final stretch. They questioned the need for a national gathering with no official party business. Now, after months of negative headlines tied to the war and rising living costs, party officials see the September 9-10 gathering as their best opportunity to rally voters behind Trump's agenda as Democrats mount a serious challenge to Republican control of both houses of Congress in the November 3 election . Some Republicans, however, remain skeptical it can meaningfully shift voter sentiment. The party officials said the event offers a platform to refocus voters on Trump's tax cuts, immigration policies and other achievements. Organizers plan to spotlight Americans they say have benefited from those policies while portraying the Democratic Party as increasingly dominated by socialist ideas and activists, according to a source familiar with the planning. The party plans to put Trump at the center of the convention, a tactic some strategists warn could backfire by drawing attention to [USN:L6N44E0VE TEXT:"a president"] with a low approval rating who has repeatedly urged Americans to endure the economic costs of the Iran war. Republican National Committee spokesperson Natalie Baldassarre said the convention would rally voters behind Trump's agenda, including efforts to lower drug prices, cut taxes and secure the southern border with Mexico. "President Trump turns out voters like no other candidate, and this convention will provide the momentum needed to expand our majorities in November," Baldassarre said in a statement. CANDIDATES FACE TRUMP CONVENTION DILEMMA It remains unclear which congressional candidates will speak during the two-day event. Advisers to three campaigns in competitive districts told Reuters they had yet to be informed whether their candidates would be offered speaking slots. Reuters contacted representatives for Republican candidates in 37 competitive U.S. House races and eight closely contested U.S. Senate races to ask whether they planned to attend the convention and deliver a speech. Of the 45, only one campaign offered a substantive response: Republican Representative Tom Barrett, seeking reelection [USN:L4N41312L TEXT:"in a tight race"] in Michigan, who plans to skip the convention and remain on the campaign trail. "He's in a tough reelection campaign and his voters are in his district," said Jason Cabel Roe, a strategist working for the Barrett campaign. Still, most of the dozen party insiders interviewed by Reuters, including convention planners and Republican National Committee members, described the convention as the party's best chance to energize Republican voters, whose enthusiasm trails that of Democrats, according to polls. "There is no better salesman for the country than Donald Trump. I don't think it's going to hurt at all," said Rob Steele, a Republican National Committeeman from Michigan. Ray Washburne, a Republican donor co-chairing the convention with his wife, told Reuters he expected about 30,000 attendees, a figure that would exceed the seating capacity of the American Airlines Center in Dallas by some 8,000 people. He said organizers raised $42 million and will fully fund the event. The timing, just at the start of the school year, could pose challenges for some attendees. One state party chair told Reuters he had returned many of his delegation's allotted seats after members said they could not make the schedule work. While declining to provide a complete speaker list, Washburne said most of Trump's cabinet secretaries would attend, along with "pretty much everyone running in a hot race." Vice President JD Vance will speak on September 9, followed by Trump on September 10. Dave Wilson, a South Carolina-based Republican strategist, said he was skeptical a rally-style convention would move the needle unless it was used to unveil a major response to voters' top concern: the cost of living. "I don't know that we're going to see a convention in Dallas change what happens in Cheyenne, Wyoming, or Charleston, South Carolina," Wilson said, invoking places far from the convention to illustrate his point. "I don't think the average Republican voter even knows there's a convention going on." CANDIDATES SEEK DONORS AND SPOTLIGHT Though it falls outside the traditional four-year presidential election cycle, the convention is expected to serve a familiar purpose as a fundraising and networking hub for candidates and donors. The RNC has already launched a website selling official convention hats, T-shirts and mugs. Washburne said the event would give candidates significant media exposure to promote their campaigns. U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton of Texas, whose campaign has been dogged by scandal, was someone who could benefit from the attention generated by a convention in his home state, Washburne added. With Trump's [USN:L6N44E0VE TEXT:"approval rating at 33%"], some Republicans questioned the wisdom of the event. One strategist working on a competitive race, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said it made little sense to tie candidates more closely to Trump when many are trying to focus on local issues and win over independent voters. Oscar Brock, an RNC member from Tennessee, said many candidates would feel obliged to attend the Dallas gathering to court donors and raise their profiles through media appearances, even as some remain wary of embracing Trump.

item.title: Bond market anxiety raises stakes for Warsh's debut Jackson Hole speech
item.description: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's debut speech at the annual Jackson Hole conference this week, self-advertised as a choice between discussing near-term policy or broader principles, has taken on added weight as traders and analysts look for guidance about the recent jump in bond yields and for reassurance of his independence from the Trump administration.
item.dc:creator: Howard Schneider
item.content:encoded: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's debut speech at the annual Jackson Hole conference this week, self-advertised as a choice between discussing near-term policy or broader principles, has taken on added weight as traders and analysts look for guidance about the recent jump in bond yields and for reassurance of his independence from the Trump administration. Warsh has said he wants to wait for recommendations from five task forces established at the start of his tenure this spring before getting too detailed about his plans. But markets have already sped towards a conclusion that the Fed's policy interest rate needs to be higher, with [USN:L1N44A0M3 TEXT:"U.S. inflation"] above the 2% target for more than five years and Warsh's colleagues concerned that if the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee doesn't hike rates to get inflation back to that level, the central bank's credibility could suffer. Globally, what former Fed Chair and Nobel Economics Prize winner Ben Bernanke deemed a "global savings glut" that kept market interest rates low has evolved into a global savings squeeze with rising government debts, fractured international trade and supply lines, the costs of population aging, and booming private investment in artificial intelligence competing to divvy up the dollars available to invest and lend. "Both the bond market and the FOMC have clearly decided to wake up" to account for higher inflation and what promises to become "a secular, multi-year uptrend in interest rates," said Adam Posen, president of the Peterson Institute for International Economics. Given the questions Warsh left open after his post-meeting [USN:L6N43Q12Z TEXT:"press conference"] last month, Posen said the Fed chief needed to dwell less on the long-term ideas he wants to pursue and more on how the central bank is evaluating the economy in the here and now along with the implications of recent global market developments. "What he should say is 'I have watched the data, listened to the market as I said I would, listened to the committee, and clearly there is reason to consider a hike in coming months if data does not change,'" Posen said. TREASURY'S LONG SHADOW Warsh is scheduled to deliver a keynote address on Friday at the Kansas City Fed's annual research symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming. The conference, with its global audience and intense media coverage, offers U.S. central bank leaders a high-profile way to set a tone or emphasize a message. Former Fed Chair Jerome Powell, for example, used the venue to unveil a new monetary policy framework, then later for a succinct, attention-grabbing pledge to fight inflation that helped cement market expectations for a series of swift rate hikes. Asked after the July 28-29 meeting about his plans for the speech, Warsh told reporters he had not decided yet, but noted his desire to "frame the big questions. There is a tendency, especially with the proliferation of meetings and press conferences, to get caught up in the myopic." But the details matter. After that press conference left key policy questions unaddressed, Warsh was already facing calls to speak more clearly about how he evaluates the risks facing the economy and the Fed's likely reaction to them, topics he has avoided because of his distaste for "forward guidance." Since then, the situation has become even more complicated. The recent jump in U.S. and global bond yields and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's decision to [USN:FWN44G0QP TEXT:"intervene in the market"] have raised the possibility that Warsh will have to account for a more activist Treasury Department and rising government debt costs — in theory not the Fed's concern unless government financing starts to stumble or Treasury's financing choices start to influence short-term interest rates. The Fed's key policy tool is an overnight interest rate, and gaps between that and short-term government debt rates, if they emerge, could make the central bank's management of rates more difficult. The impact on the value of the dollar, which has been falling over the last month against other major currencies, could also add to inflation. "We are in a regime where activist Treasury policy is as material — for good and for bad — as central bank policy. The interaction of the two will be key to the outlook," Krishna Guha, a former top New York Fed official who is now vice chairman of Evercore ISI, wrote last week as he and other analysts assessed rising bond yields. "Warsh has tried to make the unconventional case that the Fed should stand back and let the market form an unguided yield curve ... while hinting long-end tightening might be preferable to short-end tightening. It is hard to make that case when investors see Bessent as trying to manage the long end," Guha said. 'FINDING HIS FEET' Democrats on the Senate Banking Committee, meanwhile, have asked Warsh to provide details on his communications with President Donald Trump, a move that followed a Wall Street Journal report that the two men have been holding regular calls. While Trump has so far withheld [USN:L1N43V1AJ TEXT:"any criticism"] of Warsh, whom he chose for the top Fed job, for not cutting interest rates, as the president consistently demanded of Powell, Warsh's reluctance to talk about policy has left open questions about both his evaluation of the economy and whether he is holding back on his view of rate hikes to avoid angering Trump. In the [USN:L6N44G14Y TEXT:"minutes of the July 28-29 meeting"], some of Warsh's colleagues worried that waiting to hike rates would require steeper and costlier increases in borrowing costs later, while others worried that the longer inflation remains above 2% the more likely the public is to lose faith in the Fed's commitment to its target. The bond market's behavior may be reflecting those concerns, said Maurice Obstfeld, a former International Monetary Fund chief economist who is now an economics professor at the University of California, Berkeley. "He's clearly finding his feet and operating in a very charged environment," given upcoming U.S. midterm elections that could alter the final half of Trump's second term in the White House and volatile bond markets, Obstfeld said. "Markets are wondering what's the Fed going to do to address inflation that's persistently above target," he said. "There's certainly the possibility that inflation pressures lead to the need for steeper rate increases down the road, which is why you see some of this action in longer-term yields." The speech this week "is a perfect opportunity to clarify his thinking," Obstfeld said.

item.title: Trump's frustrations drove vaccine order, but MAHA wants more
item.description: Trump's frustration that his administration was not doing enough to address what he considers a likely contributor to autism drove an executive order that cut back the number of childhood vaccinations, administration officials told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Yasmeen Abutaleb, Bo Erickson
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump's frustration that his administration was not doing enough to address what he considers a likely contributor to autism drove a U.S. executive order this month that [USN:FWN4471RZ TEXT:"cut back the number of childhood vaccinations"], administration officials told Reuters. These five current and former officials privately say the order alone does not substantially change U.S. vaccine policy and will not satisfy Trump’s demands or Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s “Make America Healthy Again” political base. Instead, Kennedy and his allies are focused on a series of studies that the health secretary kicked off last year examining what they say are the dangers of vaccines, including a potential link with autism. Medical experts and scientists say such concerns have been thoroughly refuted by studies examining millions of children over many years. “No one wants to see this get done with an executive order. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. knows that will not be a lasting change if it’s not backed up by credible science,” said Del Bigtree, one of Kennedy’s longtime allies and chief executive officer of Informed Consent Action Network, a group that has continually questioned vaccine safety. “This is only the beginning of a process that had to happen.” The White House and the Department of Health and Human Services declined to comment on the specifics of what led to the executive order. White House spokesman Kush Desai said in a statement that Trump was responding to “countless parents (who) have had their questions and concerns about America’s childhood vaccine schedule ignored if not outright mocked.” HHS spokeswoman Grace Davis Jamison confirmed the research studies under way at the agency. “We are pursuing dozens of studies and analyses using some of the nation’s largest health datasets to uncover the root causes of America’s chronic disease epidemic,” Jamison said in a statement. EXPERTS WARN OF CONFUSION Leading medical groups say the Trump order will increase confusion and vaccine hesitancy among U.S. families and expose more children to preventable diseases. They fear that Kennedy’s push for vaccine safety studies is directed toward a predetermined conclusion that the shots are more dangerous than the illnesses they prevent. Trump’s vaccine order calls for reducing the federal childhood inoculation schedule to 11 immunizations from 17 and for separating the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine into three separate shots — a feat [USN:L1N44810Z TEXT:"pharmaceutical companies said could take years"]. It also directs the Justice Department to challenge state vaccination requirements for children to attend school. Kennedy [USN:L8N3Y61FI TEXT:"unveiled a similarly whittled-down"] immunization schedule in January that circumvented the normal government process for making changes to vaccine policy. A federal judge in March [USN:L1N3ZF00J TEXT:"blocked the changes,"] saying that health regulators had acted unlawfully to carry out the health secretary’s agenda. The administration is still bound by that ruling, which it is appealing. BIG PROMISES, GROWING FRUSTRATION Kennedy, an influential promoter of anti-vaccine views for decades, promised an ambitious agenda as Trump’s top health official. Soon after taking office in early 2025, he said his department would find the causes behind rising U.S. rates of autism and re-examine the safety of childhood vaccines. But Kennedy’s self-imposed deadlines on autism answers, first in September of that year, then in March 2026, came and went with no new revelations. In recent months, Trump has pressed Kennedy to deliver on his promises regarding autism in meetings at the Oval Office and in frequent phone calls. That pressure has come even as the president’s political advisers urged the health secretary early this year not to talk publicly about vaccines ahead of November’s midterm elections — a request Kennedy complied with. But Trump has remained fixated on reducing the number of vaccinations American children receive, according to the five current and former officials. In addition, Trump and Kennedy have spoken extensively about trying to find treatments and a “cure” for autism, according to the officials. The private tensions came to the fore during a July 31 televised cabinet meeting at Camp David. Trump asked Kennedy: “How are you doing on the autism research?” Kennedy replied: “We will have an answer for you.” Trump’s public questioning of Kennedy signaled to White House and health department officials that the president wanted to see immediate action, according to three senior administration officials. The [USN:FWN4471RZ TEXT:"executive order Trump announced on vaccines"] was quickly cobbled together this summer, one of the officials said. There has been a “tide shift” on discussing vaccines since the cabinet meeting, one of the officials said. “Trump and Kennedy are more synced up than they have been all year.” The studies Kennedy is overseeing examine whether the MMR vaccine produces unintended changes in the immune system, which scientists have refuted; whether autism diagnoses are linked to childhood vaccinations; a potential link between vaccines and autoimmune diseases; and the impact of thimerosal, which was removed from childhood vaccines more than two decades ago, among other studies. The work mostly relies on federal health databases that experts have warned can be misused and misinterpreted if not analyzed properly. The work is expected to take months if not longer, adding to Trump’s frustration, according to two of the officials.

item.title: Exxon turns to automated drilling in the Permian in push for higher oil output
item.description: In rural west Texas where oil rigs and pump jacks dot the sparse flat landscape, an ExxonMobil contractor sits in a small office on a drilling rig, using controls on a screen to operate robotic machinery and move tall steel pipes weighing roughly 2,000 pounds.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang
item.content:encoded: In rural west Texas where oil rigs and pump jacks dot the sparse flat landscape, an ExxonMobil (XOM.N) contractor sits in a small office on a drilling rig, using controls on a screen to operate robotic machinery and move tall steel pipes weighing roughly 2,000 pounds. This work would usually require human overseers standing on the rig floor, the most common location for accidents on a rig. Exxon, the largest oil producer by volume in the U.S., operates more than 30 drilling rigs in the Permian Basin, two of which are automated rigs with robotic equipment. By 2028, the company aims to transition half of its fleet to automated rigs to reduce the need for workers to perform potentially dangerous work and increase efficiency to drill wells faster, an executive told Reuters. The Permian Basin in Texas and New Mexico, the biggest U.S. oilfield, revolutionized energy markets two decades ago when development of the shale basin turned the U.S. into one of the leading oil-producing countries. But the relatively quick decline rate of shale wells has prompted drillers to develop more technologies to extract the oil. Some in the industry are also concerned about when the Permian's production could begin to decline. Exxon plans to [USN:L4N3XF0WI TEXT:"grow its Permian production"] by almost 40% to 2.5 million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2030. By contrast, rival oil major Chevron plans to hold production steady at about 1 million boepd, focusing instead on free cash flow. The automated drilling rigs are part of a combination of technologies and strategies Exxon is using to boost production, said Bart Cahir, Exxon's senior vice president of unconventionals, in an interview on the rig. "When we take people off the rig floor, those same individuals are now able to think ahead and plan for the next operation and that combination gives us efficiency," he said. "This is the productivity play." The company installed its first automated rig, supplied by drilling contractor Helmerich & Payne (HP.N) , last year. It drilled two miles horizontally underground in a little over six days, the third fastest time in Exxon's history. Exxon's use of automated rigs in the Permian and its goal of expanding the fleet has not been previously reported. REDUCING RISK AND DRILLING MORE On one of Exxon's automated rigs in Midland, a gate surrounds the drilling floor with a sign reading "Red Zone: Restricted Area." A drawing of the Grim Reaper illustrates the risk that workers face around heavy equipment and pressurized systems. Where workers would usually help move columns of drill pipe over two stories tall, robotic arms now position the pipes and connect them to a drill string. This allows drilling to continue deeper into the wellbore. Employees on the rig communicate with Exxon's central operations team in Houston to determine the precise movements the robotic system should make. Removing workers from the so-called Red Zones allows them to focus on other operations on the rig and reduces variability in the work, meaning more feet per day can be drilled, Cahir said. "In the history of well drilling activity, about a third of significant injuries that occur happen on the rig floor," he said. "By getting people out of that higher risk area, we're essentially eliminating that risk." Exxon plans to expand automated rigs to a quarter of the fleet next year and then half of the fleet by 2028, Cahir said. Exxon is also developing a suite of more than 40 technologies to double its oil recovery from the Permian by the early 2030s. The shale industry typically extracts just 10% of the oil in the ground due to the tight, compacted rock.

item.title: China says Middle East at critical point, calls for cooling tensions and dialogue
item.description: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday the situation in the Middle East and Gulf region had again reached a critical juncture and urged parties involved to return to dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Monday the situation in the Middle East and Gulf region had again reached a critical juncture and urged parties involved to return to dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible. Wang made the remarks in a meeting with Foreign Minister of Kuwait Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah in Beijing, according to a Chinese foreign ministry statement. Wang said "the old script of recurring conflict should not be repeated" and the top priority is to de-escalate the situation. He said China was willing to strengthen coordination with Kuwait and continue contributing to the restoration of peace and stability in the region. Tensions in the Gulf have escalated, with the U.S. preparing new economic measures targeting Iran's trade partners and Tehran threatening to halt oil exports from the waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes. The meeting came as the U.S. threatened Iran with "the greatest financial offensive ever" targeting Iran's trade partners. Iran dismissed the U.S. threat and vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf "if the economic war continues" and issued a new warning to shipping not to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission.

item.title: Eneva vende R$2,4 bi em debêntures, sendo metade ao BTG Pactual
item.description: A Eneva informou, na noite de sexta-feira, que vendeu debêntures no valor estimado de R$2,4 bilhões, 50% das quais ao BTG Pactual, que detém cerca de 26% do capital social da empresa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Eneva (ENEV3.SA) informou, na noite de sexta-feira, que vendeu debêntures no valor estimado de R$2,4 bilhões, 50% das quais ao BTG Pactual, que detém cerca de 26% do capital social da empresa. De acordo com a Eneva, foram alienadas 232.136 debêntures simples, não conversíveis em ações, em série única, da 12ª emissão da companhia, atualmente mantidas na tesouraria. O BTG Pactual vai adquirir 116.068 dessas debêntures por R$1,2 bilhão, pagos em parcela única à Eneva, que não revelou a identidade do outro comprador. "Os recursos serão utilizados integralmente para a execução do plano de liability management da companhia, mediante a liquidação antecipada de contratos de dívida que permitem o resgate antecipado facultativo total ao longo de 2026", acrescentou a Eneva.

item.title: Indonesia says death toll from August 15 earthquake reaches 100
item.description: The death toll from an earthquake that hit eastern Indonesia reached 100 on Monday, the disaster agency chief said, as relief operations continued for a 10th day.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The death toll from an earthquake that hit eastern Indonesia reached 100 on Monday, the disaster agency chief said, as relief operations continued for a 10th day. The 7.7-magnitude [USN:L6N44D00Y TEXT:"quake"] shook the province of East Nusa Tenggara on August 15, followed by thousands of aftershocks, damaging more than 73,000 homes and forcing the evacuation of about 180,000 people. The death toll reached 100 as more people undergoing treatment succumbed to their injuries, disaster agency chief Suharyanto said in a press conference, adding more than 1,600 people were injured. Authorities were distributing aid using helicopters, trucks, and motorcycles, Suharyanto said. The earthquake was Indonesia's deadliest since 2022, when a shallow 5.6-magnitude quake killed hundreds in West Java. Indonesia, an archipelago of 290 million people, straddles the "Pacific Ring of Fire", a seismically active zone where tectonic plates meet and earthquakes and volcanic eruptions are frequent.

item.title: Kremlin says British missile help for Ukraine 'adds fuel to the fire'
item.description: The Kremlin said on Monday that Britain's decision to hand Ukraine classified information on British-made components used to make SCALP long-range cruise missiles would "add fuel to the fire" and was regarded by Moscow extremely negatively.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Kremlin said on Monday that Britain's decision to hand Ukraine classified information on British-made components used to make SCALP long-range cruise missiles would "add fuel to the fire" and was regarded by Moscow extremely negatively. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham [USN:L4N44K01O TEXT:"arrived in Kyiv"] on Monday on his first overseas trip since taking office and was due to announce British support to help Kyiv improve its domestic production of long-range missiles. Asked about the visit and the support, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov accused Britain of doing everything it could to prevent any progress towards an eventual peace deal. "Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire and methodically and regularly hatches schemes to prevent even the slightest progress in the peaceful settlement process," Peskov told reporters. Peskov said that the Russian military was already systematically gathering data to identify the location of any missile production sites and then destroying them. Moscow warned London last week of unspecified "consequences" for supplying drones to Kyiv, accusing Britain of [USN:L8N44F0K7 TEXT:"deepening its involvement"] in the war following a report that British-made drones had been used for long-range strikes against Russia for the first time. Burnham said at the time that London was committed to support Ukraine 100% against "this illegal war."

item.title: AstraZeneca's blocked M&A signals tough CEO finale
item.description: The former sector leader trades at a discount to Novartis and Roche, amid growth fears. Pascal Soriot, whose 14-year tenure already counts one turnaround, ran into opposition to a union with $137 bln Bristol Myers Squibb. That leaves smaller deals, where competition is fierce.
item.dc:creator: Aimee Donnellan
item.content:encoded: There are few pharma CEOs that can match Pascal Soriot’s track record. The French-born boss took over AstraZeneca (AZN.L) in 2012, when the business was facing a painful loss of exclusivity on key drugs and a weak pipeline of future medicines. But in the years since, he fended off an audacious bid from Pfizer (PFE.N) and transformed the business into the most highly valued European drugmaker. Now the spectre of another patent cliff and investor skepticism about mega M&A mean the 67-year old CEO may need to prove himself all over again. The 9% decline faced by AstraZeneca's stock the day after The Financial Times reported it was in talks with Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY.N) was a clear thumbs down from investors on the potential deal. A [USN:L6N4400NW TEXT:"$380 billion"] combination with a rival drugmaker facing its own challenges certainly seemed risky. Yet with the deal now seemingly dead, AstraZeneca's share price is still down over 4% from the day before the report. The downbeat performance may also reflect other worries. Soriot is confident the UK-listed group is on track to reach revenue of $80 billion by 2030 and that it can keep growing after that. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha agree he can hit his 2030 target, but they also expect a steep drop-off after that as blockbuster drugs lose exclusivity. Sales are expected to fall by $10 billion between 2031 and 2035. That "patent cliff", and some disappointing clinical trials, is probably why AstraZeneca's forward price-to-earnings multiple has plummeted from over 20 earlier this year to just 15. The company now lags behind Novartis (NOVN.S) and Roche (ROPC.S) , two rivals it has historically outperformed. That suggests that buying more drugs, through M&A, is probably on the cards. Soriot may think twice about another mega deal unless his investors warm to the idea. An alternative option is to pursue smaller takeovers in areas like antibody drug conjugates ( ADCs ), which act as a kind of super chemotherapy, as well as metabolic diseases like obesity and liver disease. The good news is that AstraZeneca has a clean balance sheet and plenty of firepower: gearing up to, say, three times EBITDA would enable deals worth nearly €50 billion. The bad news is that competition is rife, given rivals like Pfizer, GSK and Novo Nordisk are also on the hunt to fill their pipelines. Pfizer paid a whopping 159% premium for Metsera last year after a tense bidding war with Novo Nordisk. AstraZeneca may face a similar battle if it targets digestible biotechs in the oncology and rare disease space where its rivals are also expanding. Soriot may fancy another revamp. Besides the BMS deal, he has a solid record for takeovers, such as the $39 billion deal for Alexion in 2021. And under his watch AstraZeneca has invested successfully in researching new drugs in-house, like lung cancer medication Tagrisso. Despite his 14-year tenure, Soriot has quashed suggestions he might stand down soon. That's good, because it may well take some time for AstraZeneca to recover its lost glory. Follow Aimee Donnellan on LinkedIn . item.title: Unternehmer und Milliardär Kühne mit 89 Jahren gestorben
item.description: Der einflussreiche Logistik-Unternehmer, Investor und Milliardär Klaus-Michael Kühne ist tot. item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der einflussreiche Logistik-Unternehmer, Investor und Milliardär Klaus-Michael Kühne ist tot. Er sei in der Nacht auf Montag an seinem Wohnort im schweizerischen Schindellegi im Alter von 89 Jahren gestorben, teilte sein Konzern Kühne + Nagel (KNIN.S) am Montag mit. Der gebürtige Hamburger und bekennende HSV-Fan galt als einer der einflussreichsten deutschen Unternehmer der Nachkriegsgeschichte. Er formte aus dem väterlichen Erbe einen globalen Logistikriesen und war zudem Großaktionär der Reederei Hapag-Lloyd (HLAG.DE) sowie der Fluggesellschaft Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) . Mit Kühne sei ein Visionär und eine eindrucksvolle Persönlichkeit gegangen, sagte der Verwaltungsratspräsident von Kühne + Nagel, Jörg Wolle. Die Gedanken seien bei seiner Witwe Christine Kühne. Konzernchef Stefan Paul erklärte, Kühne habe wie kein anderer für die Logistik und den globalen Handel gestanden. Kühne war 1958 in das Familienunternehmen eingetreten und hatte 1966 die Leitung übernommen. Ab 1975 fungierte er als Chief Executive Officer der Kühne + Nagel International AG und von 1992 bis 2011 als deren Verwaltungsratspräsident, ehe er zum Ehrenpräsidenten ernannt wurde. Unter Kühnes Regentschaft entwickelte sich das 1890 in Bremen gegründete Speditionsunternehmen zu einem weltweit führenden Logistikdienstleister. Um das Unternehmen internationaler auszurichten, verlegte er den Hauptsitz 1969 in die Schweiz, blieb seiner Heimatstadt Hamburg jedoch eng verbunden. Heute verfügt der DHL (DHLn.DE) -Konkurrent, an dem Kühne die Mehrheit hält, über knapp 90.000 Mitarbeiter und ist in fast 100 Ländern aktiv. Als die Hamburger Traditionsreederei Hapag-Lloyd im Jahr 2008 vor der Übernahme durch ausländische Investoren stand, schmiedete Kühne zudem ein Konsortium zu deren Rettung und wurde zum größten Einzelaktionär. Im Jahr 2022 stieg er bei der Lufthansa ein, wo er mit einem Anteil von 20 Prozent ebenfalls zum größten Einzelaktionär aufrückte. In Hamburg trat er zudem als streitbarer Förderer des Fußballvereins Hamburger SV (HSV) sowie als Mäzen der Elbphilharmonie auf. Kühne war nie um ein offenes Wort zum wirtschaftlichen Geschehen verlegen. Der Unternehmer hatte indes nicht mit all seinen Engagements eine glückliche Hand. Er investierte auch in die Signa-Gruppe des schillernden Immobilien-Unternehmers Rene Benko - und erlitt einen Millionenschaden. Beteiligt ist die Kühne Holding auch am Chemielogistiker Brenntag (BNRGn.DE) , an dem sie über 20 Prozent hält, an der Flixbus-Mutter Flix und am Prothesenhersteller Ottobock (OBCK.DE) . Über Immobilien verfügt die Holding unter anderem in Hamburg, Davos und Mallorca. Von der balearischen Insel war Kühne dem "Manager Magazin" zufolge jüngst in die Schweiz zurückgekehrt - sein Gesundheitszustand habe sich verschlechtert. Kühnes Vermögen, das sich Schätzungen des Magazins zufolge zuletzt auf rund 23,5 Milliarden Euro belief, solle wohl über seine gemeinnützige Kühne-Stiftung verwaltet werden. Kühne war kinderlos.

QC-Partners-Experte Thomas Altmann mahnte jedoch zur Vorsicht. "Noch kann nur spekuliert werden, was die USA heute verkünden werden. Und noch kann nur spekuliert werden, wie der Iran antworten wird." Der Rückgang beim Ölpreis belastete den Energiesektor: In Frankfurt gaben RWE (RWEG.DE) gut ein halbes Prozent nach.

item.title: Attaques de drones ukrainiens en Russie, cinq morts - autorités russes
item.description: Trois adolescents ont été tués et huit autres personnes, dont sept enfants, ont été blessées lors d'une attaque de drones ukrainiens dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi dans la région russe de Krasnodar, dans le sud de la Russie, ont indiqué les autorités russes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Trois adolescents ont été tués et huit autres personnes, dont sept enfants, ont été blessées lors d'une attaque de drones ukrainiens dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi dans la région russe de Krasnodar, dans le sud de la Russie, ont indiqué les autorités russes. Dans un message publié sur Telegram, la commissaire russe aux droits de l'enfant, Maria Lvova-Belova, a déclaré que trois adolescents, âgés de 13, 15 et 16 ans, avaient été tués, et que six autres enfants avaient été hospitalisés. Le gouverneur local, Veniamin Kondratyev, a précisé que deux adultes avaient également été blessés dans l'attaque, après que des débris sont tombés sur une crèche privée. Les débris d'autres drones ont atterri contre des immeubles résidentiels, a-t-il écrit sur Telegram, et un entrepôt du site de commerce en ligne Ozon de Krasnodar a été incendié. L'Ukraine n'a fait aucun commentaire dans l'immédiat au sujet de cette attaque. L'Ukraine a intensifié ses attaques contre les centres logistiques et les entrepôts à travers la Russie, rendant ainsi plus concrète aux yeux des civils russes la guerre déclenchée par Moscou en février 2022. Plusieurs entrepôts d'Ozon ont fait état d'attaques de drones à travers la Russie lundi et [USN:L8N44K01L TEXT:"au cours du weekend"]. Dans des déclarations publiées samedi, le président russe Vladimir Poutine a déclaré que Kyiv avait ouvert une "boîte de Pandore" en frappant des cibles économiques russes, ajoutant que Moscou riposterait en frappant les "secteurs économiques les plus sensibles" de l’Ukraine. Deux personnes ont également été tuées, et deux autres blessées, lors de frappes de drones sur la région russe de Belgorod, proche de la frontière ukrainienne, a indiqué le gouvernement régional dans un message publié sur Telegram. NOUVELLE AIDE DE L'UE À L'UKRAINE Le ministère russe de la Défense a déclaré que ses forces avaient intercepté et détruit 351 drones ukrainiens au cours de la nuit au-dessus de plusieurs régions. La Russie et l’Ukraine nient prendre délibérément pour cible des civils. Selon les Nations unies, plus de 16.000 civils, dont une large majorité d'Ukrainiens, ont été tués au cours de près de quatre ans et demi de combats. Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré lundi, à l'occasion des célébrations de l'indépendance de l'Ukraine, que Kyiv souhaitait la paix mais ne céderait pas à la Russie. "L'Ukraine souhaite absolument la paix, mais elle n'est pas prête à capituler sans condition", a déclaré le président ukrainien dans une vidéo publiée sur Telegram. Le [USN:L6N44K09L TEXT:"Premier ministre britannique"] Andy Burnham et le président du Conseil européen Antonio Costa, se sont rendus à Kyiv lundi pour assister aux événements organisés à l'occasion du 35e anniversaire de la séparation de l'Ukraine de l'Union soviétique. La Commission européenne a à cette occasion approuvé lundi une aide financière supplémentaire de 6,1 milliards d’euros destinée à l’Ukraine pour l’acquisition de nouveaux systèmes de défense

item.content:encoded: Die deutsche Entwicklungshilfe schafft einer Studie zufolge mehr Jobs in Deutschland als erwartet. Jeder Euro lasse deutsche Exporte um 2,50 Euro steigen, heißt es in einer am Montag veröffentlichten Studie der Universität Göttingen im Auftrag der Kreditanstalt für Wiederaufbau (KfW). Die Analyse untersuchte den Zusammenhang zwischen Zahlungen im Rahmen der deutschen Entwicklungszusammenarbeit und deutschen Exporten von Waren und erstmals auch von Dienstleistungen in die Partnerländer im Zeitraum von 2005 bis 2024. Den positiven Effekt begründen die Göttinger Forscher unter anderem mit Einkommenseffekten in den Empfängerländern. Diese erhöhten vor Ort Nachfrage und Importe. Davon profitiere auch die deutsche Wirtschaft: Durch zusätzlich ausgelöste Exporte seien rund 380.000 Arbeitsplätze in produzierenden Unternehmen sowie im Dienstleistungssektor in Deutschland geschaffen und gesichert worden. Die stärksten Effekte gebe es in den Sektoren Maschinenbau, Transport, Informationstechnologie, Chemie- und Elektroindustrie. Derzeit gibt es Haushaltsverhandlungen, bei denen die Bundesausgaben für Entwicklungshilfe zum fünften Mal in Folge gekürzt werden sollen. Angesichts der Rekordausgaben für Waffenkäufe stößt dies mittlerweile auch in der schwarz-roten Koalition auf Kritik. Sowohl Entwicklungshilfeministerin Reem Alibali Radovan als auch Außenminister Johann Wadephul hatten deshalb gefordert, zumindest einen Teil der Entwicklungshilfeausgaben von den Regeln der Schuldenbremse auszunehmen. Dieser Forderung schloss sich auch NRW-[USN:L8N44J02H TEXT:"Staatskanzleichef Nathanael Liminski"] am Wochenende im Reuters-Interview an.

item.title: Xpeng's robotics unit valued at over $6.3 billion after record funding round
item.description: Chinese automaker Xpeng said on Monday its robotics unit had raised more than $900 million in its first funding round, setting a new record for a single private financing in China's embodied AI sector.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese automaker Xpeng (9868.HK) said on Monday its robotics unit had raised more than $900 million in its first funding round, setting a new record for a single private financing in China's embodied AI sector. The funding round, led by IDG Capital and backed by strategic investors Tencent (0700.HK) and Alibaba (9988.HK) , values the robotics business at more than $6.3 billion, Xpeng said in a statement. The proceeds will be used to develop robotics hardware and software, train and refine physical AI models, collect high-quality data, build end-to-end mass-production facilities, and support global expansion, the company said. Xpeng plans to begin mass production of its humanoid robot, Xpeng IRON, by year-end, with initial deployments at its retail stores and industrial campuses. Commercial sales and deliveries in China and overseas markets are scheduled to begin in 2027. CEO He Xiaopeng [USN:L1N42I051 TEXT:"announced"] in June that he would personally lead the robotics business as the electric vehicle maker, seen as one of the leading automaker-backed developers of humanoid robots, pushes towards mass production. The robotics sector has attracted growing interest from automakers, which see parallels with intelligent vehicle development, including expertise in sensors, software, batteries and supply-chain management. In April, Shanghai-based embodied AI startup TARS Robotics raised more than $455 million in a pre-A funding round, a deal that was then billed as the largest single private financing in China's embodied AI sector.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Das Geschäft mit Immobilienfinanzierungen und besonders bei Gewerbeobjekten hat zuletzt spürbar angezogen. Die im Verband deutscher Pfandbriefbanken (vdp) zusammengeschlossenen Institute vergaben im ersten Halbjahr 2026 deutlich mehr Immobiliendarlehen als im Vorjahreszeitraum. Die Zusagen legten um 8,5 Prozent auf 80,4 Milliarden Euro zu, wie der vdp am Montag mitteilte. Der Löwenanteil entfiel dabei auf Wohnimmobiliendarlehen: Ihr Volumen belief sich im ersten Halbjahr auf 50,1 Milliarden Euro, ein Plus von 5,3 Prozent im Vergleich zum Vorjahreswert. Eine weit stärkere Wachstumsrate in Höhe von 14,3 Prozent wiesen Gewerbeimmobiliendarlehen auf: Ihr Volumen summierte sich von Januar bis Juni 2026 auf 30,3 Milliarden Euro. Der Zuwachs speiste sich von Januar bis Juni vor allem aus der Entwicklung bei Finanzierungen für Handelsgebäude, die im Jahresvergleich um 40,6 Prozent auf 9,0 Milliarden Euro anstiegen. Die Wachstumsraten bei der Darlehensvergabe für Büroobjekte (14,8 Milliarden Euro) und für Hotels (2,4 Milliarden Euro) betrugen 9,6 beziehungsweise 9,1 Prozent. Das Neugeschäft bei Industriegebäuden (0,5 Milliarden Euro) und bei sonstigen gewerblich genutzten Objekten (3,6 Milliarden Euro) war dagegen rückläufig im Vergleich zum ersten Halbjahr 2025. "Das Immobilienfinanzierungsneugeschäft der Pfandbriefbanken weist für das erste Halbjahr 2026 Zuwächse auf, die Entwicklung in diesem Geschäftsfeld verläuft solide", betonte Jens Tolckmitt, Hauptgeschäftsführer des vdp. Die Darlehensvergabe liege jedoch weiterhin deutlich unterhalb der Volumina, die vor der Zinswende erreicht worden seien. Für das zweite Halbjahr 2026 rechnet er unter den gegebenen Rahmenbedingungen allenfalls mit leichten Anstiegen des Neugeschäfts. Es sei davon auszugehen, dass sich die geopolitischen Unsicherheiten, die Konjunkturschwäche und die weiter angespannte Lage auf dem Wohnungsmarkt auch dämpfend auf die Immobilienfinanzierung auswirkten.

item.title: Taïwan sous des pluies torrentielles, quatre personnes portées disparues
item.description: Quatre personnes sont portées disparues après que des pluies torrentielles se sont abattues lundi sur le sud et l'est de Taïwan, entraînant la fermeture des bureaux et des écoles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Quatre personnes sont portées disparues après que des pluies torrentielles se sont abattues lundi sur le sud et l'est de Taïwan, entraînant la fermeture des bureaux et des écoles. Un système dépressionnaire stagne au-dessus du sud de Taïwan depuis quelques jours, provoquant de fortes pluies et des inondations. Et le gouvernement se prépare à l'arrivée d'un typhon qui devrait frapper l'île en fin de semaine. Les autorités de Kaohsiung, troisième ville taïwanaise avec plus de 2,7 millions d'habitants, ont déclaré qu'elles s'attendaient à ce que les précipitations cumulées sur les cinq jours de présence du système dépressionnaire dépassent 1,3 mètre, soit près de la moitié de ce que la ville enregistre habituellement en une année entière. Les pompiers taïwanais ont déclaré que sur les quatre personnes portées disparues dans les eaux de crue, trois l'étaient à Hualien et une à Tainan. TSMC (2330.TW) , le plus grand fabricant mondial de puces électroniques en sous-traitance, a dit dans un communiqué que toutes ses usines taïwanaises fonctionnaient normalement. L'administration centrale de la météorologie de Taïwan a estimé que le typhon Saudel, qui se dirige actuellement vers la région d'Okinawa, dans le sud du Japon, devrait passer au nord de Taïwan au lever du jour le vendredi avant d'atteindre la côte est de la Chine.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Iran avertit que les navires ne respectant pas les règles relatives au transit dans le détroit d'Ormuz pourraient faire l'objet de restrictions, notamment d'amendes, d'une détention ou d'une confiscation, selon un message publié sur X par l'Autorité du détroit du golfe Persique (PGSA). Cet avertissement accroît les risques pour les affréteurs et les armateurs dont les navires traversent le détroit d'Ormuz, par où transite en temps normal un cinquième du transport maritime mondial d'hydrocarbures. Le [USN:L8N44L0C1 TEXT:"volume global"] du trafic est faible, selon l'agence britannique Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), et reste inférieur d'environ 90% aux niveaux observés avant le conflit. La PGSA, une organisation nouvellement créée par l’Iran pour gérer le détroit, a invité les propriétaires de cargaisons à consulter une liste actualisée des navires jugés non conformes pour la navigation dans le golfe Persique. Les bâtiments effectuant des opérations telles que des transferts de cargaison de navire à navire ou des transbordements avec des unités non conformes seront également ajoutés à la liste des navires soumis à restriction, a précisé la PGSA. Toute demande de radiation devra être accompagnée d'explications pertinentes aux autorités maritimes iraniennes, précise le message publié sur X.

item.title: Zelenskiy says Russia is 'not ready' for ceasefire on grain ships
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia was "not ready" for a ceasefire on attacks on ships in the Black Sea carrying agricultural produce, as Moscow wants to extend any deal to cover attacks on Russian refineries and pipelines.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia was "not ready" for a ceasefire on attacks on ships in the Black Sea carrying agricultural produce, as Moscow wants to extend any deal to cover attacks on Russian refineries and pipelines. Moscow and Kyiv, major players in global agriculture markets, have accused each other of intensified attacks on vessels used for food exports during Russia's war in Ukraine . Reuters reported this month that Ukraine had sent Russia an [USN:L1N44A0XW TEXT:"offer to halt attacks"] on civilian targets in the Black Sea. [USN:L8N44B0GM TEXT:"Russia dismissed"] the idea, saying it saw no grounds for "half-measures" that would offer a respite to the other side. "I spoke with certain leaders. I proposed that they use their vessels to transport food from our ports, and we would not attack their ships if they came to pick up agricultural exports from Russia," [USN:L8N44L0A5 TEXT:"Zelenskiy"] told journalists in remarks cleared for release on Sunday. He said that Moscow, however, wanted a quid pro quo whereby it would halt attacks on Ukraine's grain corridor if Kyiv halted strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. "For (Russia), it’s not about the grain. It’s exclusively about their energy sector, but the two are not comparable," Zelenskiy said. Any deal to stop Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil refineries and fuel transportation would need to include a reciprocal cessation of attacks on Ukraine's energy system, he said. Russia, which invaded Ukraine in February 2022, did not immediately comment on Zelenskiy's remarks. [USN:S8N43I01K TEXT:"The Kremlin"] said on Monday that measures were being taken to minimise the impact of Ukraine's strikes on Russian grain exports. Ukraine has escalated its strikes on Russian economic targets in recent weeks, including on grain export terminals. Last winter, the harshest of the war, millions of Ukrainians were often left without power and heating as Russia focused its attacks on Ukraine's electricity network, leaving many apprehensive about the months ahead.

item.title: Thaïlande-Des séparatistes soupçonnés d'incendies criminels dans le sud - autorités
item.description: Des bâtiments administratifs, des commerces, des voitures et des poteaux électriques ont été incendiés au cours du week-end par des insurgés présumés, dans plus de 70 localités réparties dans quatre des provinces les plus au sud de la Thaïlande, blessant au moins trois personnes, ont déclaré lundi les autorités.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des bâtiments administratifs, des commerces, des voitures et des poteaux électriques ont été incendiés au cours du week-end par des insurgés présumés, dans plus de 70 localités réparties dans quatre des provinces les plus au sud de la Thaïlande, blessant au moins trois personnes, ont déclaré lundi les autorités. Selon celles-ci, au moins 78 incidents, dont la plupart ont eu lieu samedi soir, ont été recensés dans ces régions : 40 à Narathiwat, 21 à Yala, 15 à Pattani et deux à Songkhla. D’autres se sont produites dimanche. Aucun groupe n’a revendiqué ces attaques. Le lieutenant-général Norathip Poinok, qui commande l’armée thaïlandaise dans le sud du pays, a déclaré lundi aux médias locaux que les autorités avaient reçu, il y a près de deux mois, des renseignements les avertissant d’attaques contre des bâtiments gouvernementaux, des commerces et des infrastructures électriques. Il a également qualifié ces attaques de réponses à la répression menée contre les insurgés et les activités illicites, notamment le trafic de drogue et la contrebande, qui financent les groupes séparatistes. À Narathiwat, où un couvre-feu a été imposé, une ligne ferroviaire a été touchée par des explosifs, entraînant la suspension du trafic sur ce tronçon. Lors d’une réunion dimanche, le Premier ministre Anutin Charnvirakul a demandé aux forces thaïlandaises d’assurer la sécurité publique. Le sud du pays, à majorité musulmane et d’ethnie malaise, est confronté depuis des décennies à une insurrection visant à obtenir une plus grande autonomie ou l’indépendance. La région faisait partie du sultanat malais de Patani avant que son intégration à la Thaïlande ne soit officialisée en 1909. Plus de 7.800 personnes ont été tuées dans les provinces limitrophes de la Malaisie depuis 2004, date à laquelle la dernière vague d’une insurrection de longue date, menée principalement par le Barisan Revolusi Nasional (BRN), a éclaté. Ces attaques surviennent alors que l'État cherche à relancer les pourparlers de paix avec le BRN, le principal groupe séparatiste en lutte dans la zone. Thanut Suvarnananda, négociateur en chef, a déclaré à Reuters ce mois-ci que Bangkok souhaitait aller au-delà d’un simple échange de concessions visant à réduire la violence et s’attaquer aux griefs politiques, notamment en matière de gouvernance. Les discussions, menés sous l’égide de la Malaisie, ont connu des blocages à plusieurs reprises depuis leur lancement en 2013.

item.title: The week in Asian football
item.description: Talking points from the week in Asian football:
item.dc:creator: Michael Church
item.content:encoded: Talking points from the week in Asian football: RONALDO SCORES FROM BENCH AS AL-NASSR CONTINUE WINNING START Cristiano Ronaldo scored his first goal of the Saudi Pro League season as champions Al-Nassr picked up their second win in a row with a comfortable 4-0 victory over Al-Riyadh on Saturday. Abdulelah Al-Amri and Angelo gave Ange Postecoglou's side a two-goal lead at halftime before Joao Felix added the third and Ronaldo, introduced as a 62nd-minute substitute, completed the scoring seven minutes from time. Al-Hilal sit in second after securing a 3-0 win over Al-Fayha while Al-Ahli thrashed Abha 4-0 and Al-Ettifaq beat Al-Fateh 1-0 to all move onto six points from two matches. MACHIDA DOWN URAWA TO TOP J-LEAGUE WITH PERFECT RECORD Machida Zelvia cruised to a 3-1 win over Urawa Red Diamonds on Sunday to maintain their perfect start to the J-League season with Go Kuroda's side joined at the summit on nine points by champions Kashima Antlers and Kashiwa Reysol. Hotaka Nakamura, Takuma Nishimura and Neta Lavi were on target as Machida won for the third league match in a row to move onto nine points. Kashiwa are second after a 4-2 win over V-Varen Nagasaki while striker Leo Ceara scored at both ends in Kashima's 3-2 victory over Avispa Fukuoka. THRASHING OF ANYANG SEES SEOUL EXTEND K-LEAGUE LEAD FC Seoul handed Anyang FC a 7-0 thrashing on Saturday to increase their lead in the K-League to 13 points over second-placed Ulsan HD, who lost 1-0 to champions Jeonbuk Motors. Moon Seon-min scored twice for the league leaders against Anyang with Hrvoje Babec, Patryk Klimala, Anderson Oliveira, Jeong Seung-won and Lee Seung-mo also on target. Bruno Mota scored the only goal in the 54th minute in Jeonju as Jeonbuk defeated Ulsan to pull level with the title holders on 37 points from 24 matches. CHENGDU SEE LEAD TRIMMED AFTER LOSS IN NINE-GOAL CLASH Chinese Super League leaders Chengdu Rongcheng were on the wrong side of a nine-goal thriller on Saturday as John Aloisi's side lost 5-4 to Shanghai Shenhua to have their advantage at the top trimmed to 12 points from Beijing Guoan. He Yiran had given Chengdu a second-minute lead before Luis Asue levelled 19 minutes later, only for Wellington Silva to put the home side back in front before the interval. Two more goals by Asue either side of He's own goal put Shanghai in control and Xie Pengfei added his side's fifth in the 74th minute before two late penalties from Felipe Silva closed the gap for Chengdu.

item.title: Alibaba cae tras vender acciones por 10.200 millones de dólares para financiar su apuesta por la IA
item.description: Las acciones de la china Alibaba se desplomaban el lunes en Hong Kong después de que la compañía lanzara una venta de títulos por 10.200 millones de dólares con un fuerte descuento para financiar sus ambiciones en inteligencia artificial, mientras los inversores centraban la atención en la dilución de capital y los riesgos de ejecución.
item.dc:creator: Kane Wu, Samuel Shen, Casey Hall
item.content:encoded: Las acciones de la china Alibaba (9988.HK) se desplomaban el lunes en Hong Kong después de que la compañía lanzara una venta de títulos por 10.200 millones de dólares con un fuerte descuento para financiar sus ambiciones en inteligencia artificial, mientras los inversores centraban la atención en la dilución de capital y los riesgos de ejecución. El gigante del comercio electrónico y la computación en la nube dijo que vendería nuevas acciones por 80.000 millones de dólares hongkoneses (10.200 millones de dólares estadounidenses), a 112,70 dólares hongkoneses cada una —un descuento del 8,4% respecto del cierre del viernes—, para financiar chips, infraestructura de IA y modelos de inteligencia artificial. La IA se ha convertido en el principal motor del crecimiento de los ingresos de Alibaba en momentos en que el comercio electrónico se estanca, y sus modelos de IA Qwen figuran entre los más populares de China. Aun así, algunos inversores albergan dudas sobre el éxito que podría alcanzar la empresa. "El ADN de Alibaba está en el comercio electrónico, no en la tecnología avanzada", dijo Yang Tingwu, subdirector general de la gestora de activos Tongheng Investment. "Por mucho que invierta en 'hardware' de IA, es probable que sus competidores la aventajen en innovación tecnológica". Sus acciones en Hong Kong llegaron a caer un 10,5%, aunque reducían las pérdidas por la tarde y cotizaban en línea con el descuento ofrecido. La venta de 710 millones de acciones ordinarias equivale al 3,6% del total ampliado de títulos en circulación. La operación registró una fuerte demanda y atrajo órdenes por 28.000 millones de dólares, incluidos 6.000 millones de inversores con estrategias de largo plazo y fondos soberanos, dijeron tres personas conocedoras del asunto. Alrededor del 40% de la cartera de órdenes se adjudicará a inversores con estrategias de largo plazo y fondos soberanos, entre ellos algunos de los principales fondos soberanos de Europa, Asia y Oriente Medio, dijeron dos de las personas. Entre los inversores figuraban la Autoridad de Inversiones de Qatar (QIA), la noruega Norges y Hillhouse, según una de las fuentes. Alibaba, Hillhouse, QIA y Norges no respondieron de inmediato a solicitudes de comentarios. (1 dólar = 6,7229 yuanes chinos)

item.title: La Nouvelle-Zélande veut interdire l'accès aux réseaux sociaux aux moins de 16 ans
item.description: Le Premier ministre néo-zélandais, Christopher Luxon, a déclaré lundi que son parti allait présenter au Parlement un projet de loi visant à interdire aux enfants de moins de 16 ans d'utiliser les réseaux sociaux, la Nouvelle-Zélande étant le dernier pays en date à vouloir prendre des mesures en la matière.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le Premier ministre néo-zélandais, Christopher Luxon, a déclaré lundi que son parti allait présenter au Parlement un projet de loi visant à interdire aux enfants de moins de 16 ans d'utiliser les réseaux sociaux, la Nouvelle-Zélande étant le dernier pays en date à vouloir prendre des mesures en la matière. Ce projet de loi obligerait les plateformes de réseaux sociaux à prendre des mesures pour vérifier l'âge des utilisateurs, en s'appuyant notamment sur des informations existantes liées aux comptes, la reconnaissance faciale et des documents d'identité numériques. En cas de non-respect de l'interdiction, elles risquent des amendes pouvant atteindre 10% de leur chiffre d'affaires mondial. "Nous ne pouvons tout simplement pas accepter les dommages causés à toute une génération d'enfants néo-zélandais", déclare Christopher Luxon, cité dans un communiqué. "Les réseaux sociaux les exposent à des contenus préjudiciables, à une technologie addictive et à des pressions auxquelles ils ne sont pas préparés à faire face, ce qui affecte leur vie familiale, leur santé mentale, leur sommeil et leur éducation", poursuit-il. En décembre 2025, [USN:L8N3XG02I TEXT:"l'Australie"] est devenue le premier pays à interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 16 ans. Depuis, de nombreux Etats comme le Royaume-Uni, l'Espagne, la Pologne, la Turquie, le Brésil, l'Indonésie ont dit envisager des restrictions similaires. La France est devenue en juillet [USN:L8N43N1SY TEXT:"le premier pays européen"] à avoir mené au bout son processus législatif sur l'interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans et la mesure devait entrer en vigueur à la rentrée scolaire de septembre. Mais, il y a dix jours, [USN:L8N44B0VL TEXT:"le Conseil constitutionnel"] a censuré cette loi, jugeant qu'elle portait "une atteinte disproportionnée à la liberté d'expression" et ne garantissait pas le droit au respect de la vie privée. OPPOSITION DE L'UN DES MEMBRES DE LA COALITION AU POUVOIR Malgré l'annonce du Premier ministre néo-zélandais, il n'est pas certain que le projet de loi puisse être adopté par le Parlement, étant donné l'opposition affichée de l'un des partenaires de coalition de Christopher Luxon, le parti populiste de droite New Zealand First. La coalition gouvernementale est composée du parti de droite Le Parti National, dont est issu Christopher Luxon, qui compte le plus de sièges au Parlement, du parti libéral ACT New Zealand et de New Zealand First (Nouvelle-Zélande d'abord), parti fondé en 1993 par Winston Peters, un ancien du Parti National. "Nous sommes préoccupés par ce projet de loi, ainsi que par la direction qu'il prend et la pente glissante sur laquelle une législation de ce type mènera inévitablement notre pays", a Winston Peters, qui est également ministre des Affaires étrangères, dans un message publié sur la plate-forme X. Pour ce dernier, la décision de l'Australie de bloquer l'accès aux moins de 16 ans à des plateformes telles que TikTok, (GOOGL.O) (YouTube) d'Alphabet et (META.O) (Instagram et Facebook) de Meta a été un "échec colossal". Des chiffres du gouvernement australien, ainsi que de nombreuses études indépendantes, ont montré que plus de huit jeunes de moins de 16 ans sur dix étaient [USN:L6N44A0KP TEXT:"encore présents"] sur les réseaux sociaux au cours des trois premiers mois de l'interdiction. "Je ne vais pas prétendre que ce sera simple ni que ce sera parfait. Nous ne parviendrons pas à éloigner tous les enfants des réseaux sociaux. Certains trouveront toujours des moyens de contourner la règle, mais franchement, c'est tout simplement trop important pour ne pas au moins essayer", a dit Christopher Luxon en réaction aux critiques à son projet de loi.

item.title: Europe stitches together plan to close the loop in the fashion industry
item.description: All over the world textile waste is growing faster than anyone can cope with it. The bulk is burned, landfilled or dumped. Less than 1% is recycled into new textiles, and the cost is counted in carbon emissions, polluted waterways, and contamination by chemicals and microplastics.
item.dc:creator: Angeli Mehta
item.content:encoded: All over the world textile waste is growing faster than anyone can cope with it. The bulk is burned, landfilled or dumped. Less than 1% is recycled into new textiles, and the cost is counted in carbon emissions, polluted waterways, and contamination by chemicals and microplastics. Fast fashion and fossil-based polyester are driving the upswing in waste , forecast to rise by over 40% by 2035. It doesn’t have to be this way. Recycling technologies are being developed, but finance, policy and coordination are needed to make circularity bankable so it can scale. Robert van de Kerkhof, chief executive of industry alliance ReHubs worked to get circular textiles on the European Commission’s agenda. “It was very clear that nobody will move if there's no financial incentive – which clearly there is not – or if there's (no) legislative pressure.” That pressure is now taking shape, with expectations resting on mandated separate collection of textiles and extended producer responsibility, whereby producers pay fees to cover the costs of managing the textiles they put onto the market, adjusted for their recyclability. Alongside are export restrictions on unsorted waste and a ban on the destruction of unsold textiles. Some countries in Europe already use EPR systems for textiles including France and the Netherlands, but the EU plans for them to be in place across the bloc by January 2028. H&M told The Ethical Corporation magazine that implementation needs to be harmonised across Europe’s 27 member-states if it’s to drive transformation, but signals suggest some may go their own way. In the U.S., California is the first state to place the onus on textile and apparel companies to take responsibility once consumers are done with their products. Fees are not yet set, but penalties for non-compliance are envisaged at $50,000 a day . Women make clothes for export at a garment factory at the in Nantong, Jiangsu province, China. In large garment-making countries such as China, recyclers can source postindustrial waste as they scale. REUTERS Industry group Fashion Declares! has urged the UK government to follow suit , including developing a digital product passport to determine EPR fees and eventually drive better purchasing decisions for consumers. In particular, it wants the government to remove the de minimis customs threshold for imports, where low-value goods are allowed to enter duty-free. Europe’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) will eventually set requirements for durability, repairability and recyclability with minimum recycled content requirements. Recyclers also want to know the regulations will specify closed-loop recycling, as opposed to allowing the recycling of plastic bottles into textiles. “Without the demand signals, you don't have the financiers,” says Peter Majeranowski CEO of U.S.-based chemical recycler Circ. Global non-profit Textile Exchange has been assessing the availability of both pre- and post-consumer textiles and the capacity of recyclers both now and projected in 2030. “When we look at (ESPR) legislation, let's not just set targets without truly understanding the ecosystem and the availability of materials,” says recycling lead Adam Gardiner. Brands need this information too, he adds. “What we hear is they want to set targets but it's very difficult to know what the reality of that ecosystem may be in four or five years.” Without reliable feedstock, textile recycling can’t scale. But the infrastructure to collect, sort and pre-process textiles doesn’t exist at scale either. Another industry group, Fashion for Good, has launched an effort, backed by Adidas, Bestseller and Inditex to address the challenge. It involves the whole ecosystem from sorters to recyclers together with producer responsibility organisations (PROs) that will run EPR systems. What would it cost to scale recycling infrastructure? Modelling by ReHubs and BCG suggests that to get to a tipping point – put at 15% textile to textile recycling by 2035 – could cost between 8 and 11 billion euros in capital investment. That means recycling 2.7 million metrics tons of post-consumer waste, and collecting 8 million tons. Annual operating costs would amount to 5-6.5 billion euros. Circ, co-founded by Peter Majeranowski, has developed a new method for recycling polycotton. Earthshot Prize/Handout via REUTERS Achieving that scale requires the entire industry to move in parallel, says Van de Kerkhof of ReHubs. “EPR needs to be harmonised in order to make it easy, manageable, collectible, (and) the investments need to be orchestrated that you have enough capacities along the value chain.” He notes that European sorters and collectors are struggling financially already. “The market cannot finance this transition fast enough on its own. First-of-a-kind sorting and recycling infrastructure carries technology, volume, offtake and policy risks,” he says. Public and private capital is needed to de-risk investment, so the first industrial projects are bankable, he adds. Other countries are building collection systems. Where there’s already a big garment-making industry, such as in China, recyclers can source post-industrial waste as they scale. But on a recent visit, Textile Exchange’s Gardiner found one company offering doorstep collections of textiles, to achieve collection rates that would be considered a success story in Europe. U.S. waste management group WM is also piloting doorstep collections. “On a broader scale, it's about how can you tap into pre-existing (collection) infrastructure and networks to not have to completely rebuild the wheel,” he suggests. Even with the scale of investment anticipated in Europe, recycled fibres will be at a price premium. Consultancy Systemiq calculated that the cost of recycled polyester is around 2.6 times that of new polyester. That means brands will either have to absorb the costs or pass them on to consumers. ReHubs suggests that for a 10-euro T-shirt made of polyester, that could translate to a 60-cent price increase. Dhaka-based Harnest has creating a Responsible Trims platform, working with recyclers to create labels, elastics and threads. Harnest/Handout via REUTERS Renewcell, a Swedish pioneer of cotton recycling, found brands weren’t willing to pay the premium for its fibres. Filing for bankruptcy in 2024, before it could scale, its chairman Michael Berg said the decision was “a testament to the lack of leadership and necessary pace of change in the fashion industry”. The Ethical Corporation spoke to Renewcell in 2018, when the first fibres were coming off its production line. Back then it flagged the issue of collection and sorting infrastructure. But the business is now back as Circulose (the name of its product) and planning to re-open its Swedish plant. The difference this time is that during the scale-up phase brand partners will pay a license fee to access its fibres: Marks & Spencer, Mango and a former backer H&M are amongst them. For textile-to-textile recycling to scale, brands also need to commit to offtake agreements, and recycling needs to grow in parallel with collection and sorting. “I think of Circ now less as an innovation company and more of a coordination company, where we are building the circular economy. All the ingredients are on the kitchen counter, and we have to put them together to make the final meal,” says Majeranowski of Circ. Manufacturing waste and heavy textile users like hotels and restaurants will be an initial source of recycled materials, ahead of post-consumer recycling, says Majeranowski. “We can’t recycle what isn’t already collected (and) we need to demonstrate to bankers that we have a dependable source.” Circ has set up a “fiber club” to address volume and price considerations by aggregating demand pre-competitively amongst brands to meet minimum order quantities for pilots. They’ve worked with fibre producers Birla and Lenzing, and yarn producers, so brands have the material to work with. Fashion “is a very conservative business: Fiber Club is another way to help them take that first leap,” says Majeranowski. A man sorts offcuts of fabric that will be sold to textile factories before being recycled, in the outskirts of Faisalabad, Pakistan. REUTERS/Fayyaz Hussain In preparation for its first plant, expected to come online in France in 2028, Circ is using demo-level fibres to qualify them with the various spinners, knitters and weavers that brands rely on, creating a library of fabric constructions that buyers can select from. One of the tensions in building circular systems is that sorters and recyclers are dealing with products that were never intended for disassembly or recycling, observes Azra Cevapovic, innovation manager at Fashion for Good. Trims is one often-overlooked area. “Circularity won't scale through fabric alone, and the smaller components are where it usually breaks down,” says Assef Shaikh, chief executive of Dhaka-based Harnest. It’s created what it calls a Responsible Trims platform, working with recyclers such as Indorama and Amber Cycle to create labels, elastics, threads, drawcords and dyed yarns that match the fabrics they’re used with. All the processing stages are carried out under one roof, so it can offer its recycled trims at cost-parity with virgin materials. “We're trying to address a problem in the entirety of a garment,” says Shaikh. “If your elastic (or) your thread is not recycled, then recycling it further (is) a problem,” as additional processing is required. Shaikh advocates for complete mandatory material disclosure across the entire garment and to include trims in EPR calculations to boost textile-to-textile recycling. As a centre of garment manufacture, Bangladesh also has the potential to create a big recycling sector. The U.N. Industrial Development Organisation (Unido) has been working with H&M and Circ, testing its recycling process with H&M suppliers in Bangladesh. The same handful of brands are innovating across the recycling ecosystem, but Majeranowski is optimistic that more will join them. “The rest are watching closely, and I think will follow very quickly.” The disruption to supply chains by recent geopolitical events is having an impact, he says. “Circularity is really now about resilience and insurance.” This article is part of The Ethical Corporation's in-depth briefing on the circular economy.
